texts.preamble: State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 In The Court Of Ms. Pranjali Prakash, Judicial Magistrate First Class (Digital Traffic Court) North-East District, Karkardooma Court Complex, Delhi Tc No.: 7871/2022 Cnr No. Dlne020128672022 State Versus Dheeraj Gupta 1 . Name & address of the accused : Dheeraj Gupta, S/o Jai Kumar Gupta, R/o WZ-37, Om Vihar, Phase-III, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi-110059. 2.
texts.facts: Brief Facts: 2. It has been alleged by the Prosecution that on 14.01.2021 at about 07:34 pm, at Iron Bridge, Delhi falling within the jurisdiction of Gandhi Nagar Traffic Circle, the accused was using his vehicle bearing number DL2CAU2370 without registration and was found carrying excess passenger and putting his private vehicle to commercial use and was also found using an alter seat in his vehicle State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/ 1 and, therefore, was challaned for RC Violation under Section 39/192 of M.V. Act, 1988. 3. It is pertinent to mention here that the cognizance of the offence had already been taken by Virtual Traffic Court and a fine was proposed for the summary disposal of the case under Section 208, M.V. Act. The accused exercised the option to contest the present challan on the web portal of Virtual Traffic Court, pursuant to which the present challan was transferred to this Court for adjudication as per law. Proceedings before the Court: 4. Accused Dheeraj Gupta, entered his first appearance before this Court on 19.12.2024. Notice under Section 251 Cr.P.C. was framed against him on 03.05.2025 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. The accused pleaded that he had sold off his vehicle bearing no. DL-2CAU-2370 in the year 2016 to Regents PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2026.01.08 TC No. 7871/2022 State vs. Dheeraj Gupta 14:20:14 -0300 Automobiles and he did not have the possession of the said vehicle at the time of the offence. He further pleaded that he does not know how this vehicle came to be challaned in his name. It was thus pleaded by him that he has not committed any offence in violation of the provisions of the M.V. Act and the present challan has been wrongly issued against him by the Traffic Police. 5. In order to prove its case, the Prosecution wished to examine one witness PW-1, Retired. SI Narender Tyagi, S/o Late Sh. Kishori Lal. PW-1, in his examination-in-chief deposed that on 14.01.2021, he was posted at Gandhi Nagar Circle as ZO. On that day, a vehicle bearing no. DL-2CAU-2370 was driven by a person, namely, Ankit without registration. The said driver was carrying 11 passengers in his vehicle exceeding the capacity and was found misusing his vehicle by putting it to commercial use. He further deposed that he issued a challan and the same is exhibited as Ex. PW1/A & Ex. PW1/B. He further deposed that he took the signature of driver Ankit at point B. The duplicate challan regarding the abovesaid original challan as Marked A-1. 6. In his cross-examination, PW1, denied the suggestion that the vehicle has been handed over to Regent Autolinks Pvt. Ltd. 7. After completion of Prosecution Evidence, the statement of accused was recorded on 10.11.2025 under section 351 BNSS wherein the entire incriminating evidence appearing against the accused was put to him to which he stated that the challan has PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2026.01.08 TC No. 7871/2022 State vs. Dheeraj Gupta 14:20:21 -0300 been wrongly issued in his name and that he had handed over the vehicle in question to Regent Autolinks Pvt. Ltd. in the year 2016. 8. Thereafter, the matter was listed for Defence Evidence. Accused examined himself as DW-1 and in his defence he placed on record his bank statement of September, 2016 reflecting the transactions made in his account by the insurance company when his vehicle was destroyed in an accident in State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/ 2 June, 2016. He further deposed that the insurance company after returning the insured amount took the RC, duly signed Form 36 (sale letter form) and Bank NOC and the same is exhibited as Ex.DW1/A. Appreciation of Evidence:
texts.arguments: 10. In the present case, a violation of section 39 of M.V. Act has been alleged which reads as:- Necessity of Registration:- "No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place or in any other place unless the vehicle is registered in accordance with this Chapter and the certificate of registration of the vehicle has not been suspended or cancelled and the vehicle carries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed manner: PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2026.01.08 TC No. 7871/2022 State vs. Dheeraj Gupta 14:20:27 -0300 PROVIDED that nothing in this section shall apply to motor vehicle in possession of a dealer subject to such conditions as may be prescribed by the Central Government". 11. In the present case, a violation of section 192 of M.V. Act has been alleged which reads as:- Using vehicles without registration:- (1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or cause or allows a motor vehicle to be used contravention of the provisions of section 39 shall be punishable for the first offence with a fine which may extend to five thousand rupees but shall not be less than two thousand rupees for a second or subsequent offence with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees but shall not be less than five thousand rupees or with both: PROVIDED that the court may, for reasons to be recorded, impose a lesser punishment. (2) Nothing in this section shall apply to the use of a motor vehicle in an emergency for the conveyance of persons suffering from sickness or injuries or for the transport of food or materials to relieve distress or of medical supplies for a like purpose: PROVIDED that the person using the vehicle reports about the same to the Regional Transport Authority within seven days from the date of such use. (3) The court to which an appeal lies from any conviction in respect of an offence of the nature specified in sub-section (1), may [LEAKAGE_MASK] or vary any order made by the court below, notwithstanding that no appeal lies against the conviction in connection with which State vs Dheeraj Gupta on 8 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52925131/ 3 such order was made. PRANJALI by PRANJALI PRAKASH PRAKASH Date: 2026.01.08 14:20:33 -0300 3[Explanation: Use of a motor vehicle in contravention of the provisions of section 56 shall be deemed to be a contravention of the provisions of section 39 and shall be punishable in the same manner as provided in sub-section (1).]
